ground_truth.unit: logit coefficient per real dollar of sugar-industry contributions
ground_truth.location: Table 1, District fixed effects, Inflation-adjusted sugar contributions
ground_truth.context: Table 1 ("The Determinants of Voting in Favor of Sugar Reform"), column District fixed effects, row Inflation-adjusted sugar contributions.  Logit; the dependent variable equals 1 for "aye" votes on the two reform amendments to the U.S. sugar program (the 2013 Pitts amendment, H. Amdt. 227 to H.R. 1947, and the 2018 Foxx amendment, H. Amdt. 605 to H.R. 2; aye = a vote against sugar interests) and 0 otherwise.  One observation per House district and vote; the two votes are treated as repeated votes on the same issue. Regressor: inflation-adjusted sugar-industry contributions (all sugar-industry PACs plus individual contributions over $200 from people working in the sugar industry, Center for Responsive Politics) to the incumbent, aggregated from one year before the vote through the end of the calendar year of the vote.  Controls: the American Conservative Union ideology score (ACU, 1-100, higher = more conservative), tenure, the district poverty rate, % with a bachelor's degree, median income, % population over 65, and a dummy for membership on the House agriculture committee.  District fixed effects, so only the districts whose vote outcome changed between the two amendments identify the coefficients.  Probability values from robust standard errors; the table prints coefficient (p), p = 0.001, significant at 1%.

i4r.notes: DP 57 Table 1 col 1 (robust SEs reproduction), -0.0006, p < 0.001.

Robust standard errors; the table prints p = 0.001, significant at 1%.

i4r.notes: DP 57 Table 1 col 2, -0.0004, p < 0.001 (the meta-database row's r_coeff "-.004" is a slip).

cell.label: claude-code
deviations_manifest: Contributions in the data are nominal; inflation-adjusted to 2018 dollars with CPI-U annual averages (2013: 232.957, 2018: 251.107). The paper does not state the base year or deflator.

Window-to-file mapping: SugarReplicate.dta = baseline window (verified as the superset window); SugarReplicate_iter1.dta assumed = calendar-year window and SugarReplicate_iter2.dta = 12-months-before window, following the order the windows are described in the text/Table 3. The data alone gave mixed evidence on this assignment.

Fixed-effects logit estimated as an unconditional logit with district (or incumbent) dummies on the vote-switching sample (the paper's table reports a constant and pseudo R2, as Stata logit with i.dummies does); robust (sandwich, n/(n-1)) SEs. A conditional logit gives roughly half-size coefficients (printed as a side check only).

The contribution regressor is the window-specific author-aggregated variable totalcont (differs across the three files); sugcont is identical across files and is taken to be the election-cycle aggregate, not used.
cell.notes: Outcome y=1 if vote=='Aye', 0 otherwise (No, Not Voting, No Vote). District sample: districts with two rows whose y differs, complete covariates (94 switchers, 93 after one with missing data) -> 186 obs. Incumbent sample: those switching districts with both==1 (same member both votes) -> 53 incumbents (47 aye->not-aye, 6 no->aye), 106 obs; FE = incumbent (equivalently the district within this sample). Controls: ACU (ncu), tenure, poverty, bach, medincome, over65, agcom. agcom is quasi-separated (large coefficient, undefined SE) as in the paper; the reported quantities are unaffected. Attempts 1-3 were exploratory (data structure, file/window mapping, sample counts) and printed no RESULT lines. The Replication Read Me.docx (data documentation in the mount) was read; no script or output files exist in the mount.
